rubrics.name: Findable
rubrics.rationale: PID present (scheme: DOI); PID resolved; deposited in a sustainable repository (Zenodo); that the PID resolves to a specific VERSION of the dataset is not verified — confirm before accepting (the gate requires a 2 here)

rubrics.name: Accessible
rubrics.rationale: metadata fetchable via PID lookup; standard vocabularies referenced: MeSH

rubrics.name: Interoperable
rubrics.rationale: metadata is JSON-LD; standard vocabularies referenced: MeSH

rubrics.name: Reusable
rubrics.rationale: machine-readable license linked in the metadata (Apache-2.0); no AI/ML prohibition language found in license or use terms

rubrics.name: Transparent
rubrics.rationale: 6 datasets carry provenance links; ground-truth elements missing: samples, instruments

rubrics.name: Traceable
rubrics.rationale: 5 machine-readable transformation steps; every computation links its software; completeness of the provenance record (or disclosure of known gaps) is asserted, not verified; final score is capped at 1.a's score (rule 1.b ≤ 1.a)
rubrics.capped_by: dependency rule 1.b ≤ 1.a: score lowered from 2 to 1

rubrics.name: Interpretable
rubrics.rationale: 1 of 5 archived with a PID; 4 on mutable code hosting only

rubrics.name: Key actors identified
rubrics.rationale: 1 of 2 authors carry a PID; 1 named in free text only

rubrics.name: Semantics
rubrics.rationale: abstract present (695 chars — length-checked only, not read for substance); 12 keywords; 4 controlled-vocabulary terms

rubrics.name: Statistics
rubrics.rationale: 6 entities carry a summary-statistics link; missing-data statement present (its consistency and domain-appropriateness are asserted, not verified against the files)

rubrics.name: Standards
rubrics.rationale: 1 schema entities; standard vocabulary bindings populated: Croissant, Wikidata

rubrics.name: Data documentation template
rubrics.rationale: human-readable datasheet linked; 8 of 9 machine-readable sections populated (presence-checked only — whether coverage is substantive is a human read)

rubrics.name: Fit for purpose
rubrics.rationale: appropriate and inappropriate uses both stated; 1 prior publications linked

rubrics.name: Verifiable
rubrics.rationale: checksums on all 6 datasets and software (embargoed excluded)

rubrics.name: Secure
rubrics.rationale: confidentiality level is an HL7 v3-Confidentiality code ('M'); whether the declared level is actually ENFORCED (the 0-rule) is not verified — score 0 if controlled data is retrievable without authorization or authorized users are blocked

rubrics.name: Persistent
rubrics.rationale: PID present (scheme: DOI); recognized archive(s): Zenodo; an explicit retention commitment is assumed for recognized repositories, not verified; note the criterion covers RAW/unprocessed data — confirm the raw data itself is what's archived

rubrics.name: Associated
rubrics.rationale: components associated machine-readably in the archived metadata record (hasPart / distribution + provenance links); accessibility of every component not verified — downgrade if pieces are missing

rubrics.name: Standardized
rubrics.rationale: declared standards: Croissant, Dublin Core, W3C PROV-O, schema.org; deterministic validator known: Croissant — mlcroissant validator; JSON Schema — any JSON Schema validator (e.g. python-jsonschema); PROV-O — PROV-CONSTRAINTS validation (ProvToolbox `provconvert -validate`); populated vocabulary bindings present (final score is capped at 2.c's score — rule 6.a ≤ 2.c)

rubrics.name: Contextualized
rubrics.rationale: machine-readable example dataset provided; withheld/preprocessing information described; splits N/A unless the dataset should define them — reviewer to confirm

note: Only criteria with an automated estimate are counted; the rest need human or model judgment and are listed in unestimated_criteria.
